SMCI
Trade SMCI on Coinbase

Super Micro Computer Inc (NASDAQ:SMCI) stock is down 2.8% to trade at $34.79 at last glance, pacing for a fourth session decline out of six as the chip producer attempts to bounce back from last week's two-month low. The stock has shed 32% since its annual high of $51.40, however a historically bearish signal is now flashing on the charts.

smci chart

SMCI sports a 10-day call/put volume ratio of 4.99 at the International Securities Exchange (ISE), Cboe Options Exchange (CBOE), and NASDAQ OMX PHLX (PHLX), which stands higher than 90% of readings from the past year. There have been nine instances in the last three years that the equity's 10-day buy-to-open call/put ratio crossed over 1.0 and moved into the 90th percentile.

Per Schaeffer's Senior Quantitative Analyst Rocky White, the fintech name was higher one month later 33% of the time after these signals, averaging an 12.5% loss. A move of similar magnitude would place the stock at $30, back near those lows.

Super Micro steps into the earnings confessional after the market closes on Tuesday, Nov. 3. SMCI has scored three-straight double digit post-earnings moves higher, but has finished lower in eight of the last 12 post-earnings reports. Regardless of direction, the stock averages a 14.2% move.

Nutanix recently paired strong Q2 results with new AI-focused alliances, including Supermicro and Netris, aimed at simplifying enterprise and neocloud AI infrastructure.

The mix of better-than-expected quarterly performance and concrete AI stack offerings positions Nutanix squarely in the thick of hybrid-cloud and VMware exit spending decisions.

We will look at how Nutanix's investment narrative is shaped by its stronger Q2 delivery and deeper AI infrastructure partnerships.

Spot 55 AI infrastructure stocks that, like Nutanix, are tied directly to real AI infrastructure spending and could be next in line for investor attention.

Nutanix Investment Narrative Recap

The big belief with Nutanix is that it can turn its hybrid cloud and AI platform into a long term subscription engine, even as more workloads move to public cloud providers. The short term story hinges on converting recent Q2 momentum and AI buzz into durable annual contract value, while keeping operating discipline tight after a very large earnings jump.

The biggest near term swing factor is how effectively Nutanix captures VMware exit and AI infrastructure projects without letting sales and R&D spending run ahead of demand. The main risk is that competition, pricing pressure, and any slowdown in customer expansion blunt net retention, which would make recent margin strength harder to sustain.

The Supermicro alliance around Nutanix Agentic AI is the clearest operational tie in to the current AI narrative. It packages Nutanix Cloud Platform, Supermicro servers, NVIDIA GPUs, Nutanix Unified Storage, and Kubernetes into a ready to deploy inference stack. That speaks directly to enterprise buyers that want private AI, but do not want to assemble dozens of vendors.

For catalysts, this kind of full stack offer gives Nutanix a way to compete for larger AI infrastructure budgets rather than just selling core HCI software. Execution risk is real. Nutanix still has to prove it can scale GPU ready clusters efficiently, manage support complexity with partners, and do all of that while keeping margins and operating expenses under control.

Nutanix's narrative projects US$4.2b revenue and US$673.9m earnings by 2029. That implies 13.8% yearly revenue growth and an earnings decline of about US$826m from current earnings of US$1.5b.

title: Super Micro Is Down 32% in a Year. Is It Time to Sell, or Load Up?
detail:
Super Micro Is Down 32% in a Year. Is It Time to Sell, or Load Up?
Rexielyn Diaz
Wed, October 28, 2026 at 6:35 AM EDT 5 min read
SMCI
Trade SMCI on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Super Micro Is Down 32% in a Year. Is It Time to Sell, or Load Up? ©Edgar G. Biehle from Getty Images via Canva
Key Takeaways

Super Micro stock is down 32% over the past year after a revenue miss, an export-control indictment of people tied to the company and a $5.6 billion stock sale.

The business has improved: fiscal 2026 sales rose 78% to $39.1 billion, and preliminary September-quarter sales beat its own guidance by about $4 billion.

Growth has come at a cost: free cash flow was negative $7.0 billion in fiscal 2026, and the share count is still rising.

At 7.5x forward earnings, the stock looks too cheap if the Nov. 3 report confirms the early numbers.

Super Micro Computer (SMCI:NASDAQ) stock is down 32% in the past year (through Tuesday's close), even though the company just said its September quarter came in about $4 billion above its own guidance.

Investors got burned three times

It started in November 2025, when fiscal first-quarter sales of $5.0 billion missed guidance of $6 billion to $7 billion.

The December quarter swung the other way: sales hit $12.7 billion, but one data center customer took about 63% of revenue, and gross margin sank to 6.3%.

Then in March, the Justice Department charged three people tied to Super Micro, including a co-founder. Prosecutors say they diverted about $2.5 billion of U.S. AI technology to China. The company wasn't named as a defendant, but the stock lost a third of its value on March 20.

And in June, Super Micro raised $5.6 billion by selling common stock and mandatory convertible preferred. The common went out at $27.50 a share, a year after the company bought back stock at $40.89. (Not great timing.)

TIKR tracks 18 analysts on Super Micro Computer. How many say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Super Micro Computer, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Super Micro Computer's Analyst Ratings

Meanwhile, the business got much better

Gross margin climbed from 6.3% in the December quarter to 9.9% in March and 17.5% in June. That quarter, enterprise and channel customers made up half of sales.

Fiscal 2026 sales rose 78% to $39.1 billion, and new orders topped $60 billion. Management guided fiscal 2027 sales to $65 billion to $72 billion.

CEO Charles Liang credits the customer mix: "As demand accelerates, we are improving profitability through a richer enterprise customer mix."

Still, one-time items and deals that slipped into later quarters helped June's margin, so 17.5% isn't the new baseline.

Then came the Oct. 20 update: estimated September-quarter sales of $18.5 billion to $19.5 billion. That's nearly four times the year-ago quarter and well above the $15.23 billion analysts expected. The estimated 12.0% to 12.5% gross margin beat guidance, too.

And for the full year? Analysts expect $70.0 billion of fiscal 2027 revenue, near the top of management's range.

Super Micro Computer (SMCI): revenue, actual and consensus estimates, $ billions, fiscal 2024–2029 (years to June) (TIKR)

(Some of June's margin came from one-time items and from deals that slipped into later quarters, so 17.5% isn't the new baseline.)

Shareholders paid for the growth

Growth this fast eats cash: free cash flow was negative $7.0 billion in fiscal 2026. Dilution isn't new, either. The share count was rising well before the raise…

Super Micro Computer (SMCI): diluted shares outstanding, millions of shares, fiscal 2021–2025 (years to June) (TIKR)

It's still climbing: 697 million in fiscal 2026, and 745 million guided for the September quarter.

Nor has the legal cloud lifted. In August, a board-led investigation found no evidence that current senior management knew of the alleged scheme. But a former contractor pleaded guilty on Oct. 8, and co-founder Wally Liaw goes to trial in March 2027.

Cheap for a reason, and still too cheap

All of that leaves Super Micro at 7.5x forward earnings. That's roughly half its five-year average of 14.7x.

Super Micro Computer (SMCI): forward (NTM) P/E, last 5 years (TIKR)

And analysts still expect normalized EPS to rise 29% in fiscal 2027, to $4.67. The $43 consensus target sits about 21% above Tuesday's close. Even Underperform-rated BofA raised its target to $38 on Oct. 21.

The market is pricing in the next blow-up while sales run far ahead of guidance. At this price, I'd load up.

The next check is Nov. 3, when Super Micro reports final September-quarter results. Watch whether final figures land in the preliminary ranges and whether operating cash flow is positive.

Of course, another legal headline or an AI-spending scare like this month's could widen the discount fast.

Forrester Research recently ranked Palantir as a leader in AI platforms, and Sanjit Singh at Morgan Stanley sees Palantir emerging as the standard in enterprise AI.

The bull case centers around unique software. Whereas traditional analytics tools feature dashboards that tell clients what is happening, Palantir goes further. Its software revolves around a decision-making framework that helps customers decide what should happen next, and it lets them execute actions within the platform.

Palantir is also popular for providing flexibility and supporting privacy. Its AI platform gives customers the freedom to deploy the large language models of their choosing and swap between models without rewriting underlying applications. Palantir's software also includes governance controls that ensure business data is never fed back to model developers.

The bear case for Palantir is entirely focused on its valuation. Despite impressive financial results -- revenue increase 93% in the second quarter, the 12th consecutive acceleration -- Palantir currently trades at 78 times sales, making it the most expensive stock in the S&P 500 by a wide margin. The next closest contender is CrowdStrike at 50 times sales.

Indeed, Brent Thill says Palantir has excellent fundamentals, but the valuation simply does not make sense. He also thinks the company may be underinvesting in future growth, citing its high margins as evidence. But Thill is in the minority on Wall Street, as most analysts think the stock is undervalued. Palantir has a median target price of $223 per share, implying 12% upside from its current share price of $199.
